parts.latex: Which of the following is equivalent to the true bearing of $250^\circ$?

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{497_q9_s1}

A true bearing of $250^\circ$ is measured clockwise from north.

Since $180^\circ < 250^\circ < 270^\circ$, the direction lies between south and west.

It is past south by
$$250^\circ - 180^\circ = 70^\circ$$
towards the west, so the direction is $\text{S}70^\circ\text{W}$.

Options A and C are not valid compass-bearing forms, and $\text{S}20^\circ\text{E}$ is $160^\circ$.
$$\therefore\ \text{S}70^\circ\text{W (option D)}$$

497_q9_s1.notes: New sketch drawn from the worked solution. O at the centre with labels N (solid north line), S, E and W (dashed). The ray at bearing 250° (S70°W) goes into the SW quadrant. The outer clockwise arc with an arrowhead runs from N to the ray, labelled 250°. The inner clockwise arc runs from N to S, labelled 180°. A small arc between S and the ray is labelled 70°. In round 2 the arc radii were enlarged so that every label sits clear of the arcs and lines. Rules 3, 4, 11, 14, 22.

parts.latex: The bearing from $O$ to $P$ is $S57^\circ E$. Which is the compass bearing to $O$ from $P$?

solutions.latex:
From $O$, the point $P$ lies $57^\circ$ east of south.

The return direction from $P$ to $O$ is exactly opposite: north becomes south and east becomes west, with the same angle.

So the bearing from $P$ to $O$ is $N57^\circ W$.

The question asks for the compass bearing, so the answer is $N57^\circ W$ (the equivalent true bearing is $303^\circ$, but that is not in compass form).

Hence the answer is option B.

meta.self_check: Reverse of S57E is N57W = 360-57 = 303 true bearing; compass-form option is B.

Town $B$ is 45 km due north of town $A$ and 30 km from town $C$. Town $A$ is 39 km from town $C$.

Not to Scale

What is the bearing of town $C$ from town $B$?

solutions.latex:
In triangle $ABC$, use the cosine rule to find $\angle CBA$:
$$\begin{aligned}\cos B &= \dfrac{a^2+c^2-b^2}{2ac} \\ &= \dfrac{30^2+45^2-39^2}{2\times 30\times 45} \\ &= \dfrac{13}{25} \\ \angle CBA &= 58.66\ldots^\circ\end{aligned}$$
BA points due south from $B$ (bearing $180^\circ$), and $C$ is further round, so
$$\text{bearing} = 180^\circ + 58.66\ldots^\circ = 239^\circ \text{ (to the nearest degree)}$$
This is option C.

solutions.latex:
The $48^\circ$ at $A$ is measured from due south ($AC$), so the bearing of $B$ from $A$ is
$$180^\circ - 48^\circ = 132^\circ$$
The bearing of $A$ from $B$ is the reverse direction.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Bearing of } A \text{ from } B &= 132^\circ + 180^\circ \\ &= 312^\circ \end{aligned}$$
So the correct option is D.

6269.stem:
Two hikers decide to leave a campsite ($C$) to visit some landmarks in the area. One hiker walks 26 km on a bearing of $065^\circ$T to see a lake ($L$), the other hiker walks 16 km on a bearing of $285^\circ$T to see a mountain ($M$).

\exfigure{496_q32_1}

figures.cap: campsite C with bearings to lake L and mountain M

parts.latex: Show that $\angle MCL = 140^\circ$.
Calculate the distance between the Mountain ($M$) and the Lake ($L$), correct to the nearest kilometre.

Hence, find the bearing of the lake from the mountain.

Give your answer correct to the nearest degree.

solutions.latex:
The angle is made up of the bearing $065^\circ$ and the angle from north back to $285^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned} \angle MCL &= 65 + (360 - 285) \\ &= 65 + 75 \\ &= 140^\circ \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

solutions.latex:
Let $x = ML$. Using the cosine rule in $\triangle MCL$:
$$\begin{aligned} x^2 &= 16^2 + 26^2 - 2(16)(26)\cos 140^\circ \\ &= 256 + 676 - 832\cos 140^\circ \\ &= 1569.34897\ldots \\ x &= 39.61500\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{distance} \approx 40 \text{ km}$$
criteria: Substitutes into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

solutions.latex:
The bearing of $C$ from $M$ is the reverse of $285^\circ$, but measured from the north at $M$ it is
$$\begin{aligned} \text{bearing of } C \text{ from } M &= 90 + 15 \\ &= 105^\circ \end{aligned}$$
Let $\theta = \angle CML$. Using the sine rule:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{\sin\theta}{26} &= \dfrac{\sin 140^\circ}{39.615\ldots} \\ \theta &= \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{26\sin 140^\circ}{39.615\ldots}\right) \\ &= 24.95\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{bearing from } M \text{ to } L &= 105 - 25 \\ &= 080^\circ \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the angle $CML$, or equivalent merit
Finds the bearing of $C$ from $M$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: Which compass bearing is equivalent to $210^\circ\text{T}$?

solutions.latex:
A bearing of $210^\circ\text{T}$ is measured clockwise from north. It lies between $180^\circ$ (south) and $270^\circ$ (west), so the compass bearing is measured from south towards west.
$$\begin{aligned} 210^\circ-180^\circ &= 30^\circ \end{aligned}$$
So the direction is $30^\circ$ from south towards west, that is S$30^\circ$W.

Options A and C point towards the east, and D is $60^\circ$ from south, so they are incorrect.
$$\therefore\ \text{S}30^\circ\text{W}$$

6381.stem:
A helicopter leaves Underwood and flies 70 km on a bearing of $055^\circ$ to Vanna Beach.

It then flies 82 km on a bearing of $150^\circ$ to Weston.

The diagram below illustrates the journey.

\exfigure{308_q21_1}

figures.cap: bearings diagram U to V to W
solution diagram (drawn by Claude)

parts.latex:
It then plans to fly directly back to Underwood.

Calculate the distance that it will fly.
Determine the bearing (from Weston) on which it should fly to return to Underwood.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{308_q21_s1}

The return flight is side $UW$ of triangle $UVW$. First find $\angle UVW$.

The bearing of $U$ from $V$ is $055^\circ+180^\circ=235^\circ$ (co-interior angles with the north lines), and the bearing of $W$ from $V$ is $150^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned} \angle UVW &= 235^\circ-150^\circ \\ &= 85^\circ \end{aligned}$$
Apply the cosine rule in triangle $UVW$.
$$\begin{aligned} UW^2 &= UV^2+VW^2-2\cdot UV\cdot VW\cos 85^\circ \\ &= 70^2+82^2-2\times 70\times 82\times\cos 85^\circ \\ &\approx 10\,623.5 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} UW &\approx 103.07 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the helicopter flies about } 103 \text{ km}$$

meta.self_check: Computed in python: UW = 103.07 km; angle 85 degrees from bearings.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{308_q21_s1}

Find $\angle UWV$ using the sine rule in triangle $UVW$.
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{\sin \angle UWV}{70} &= \dfrac{\sin 85^\circ}{103.07} \\ \sin \angle UWV &= \dfrac{70\sin 85^\circ}{103.07} \\ \angle UWV &\approx 42.6^\circ \end{aligned}$$
The angle is acute because $UV<VW$, so $\angle UWV$ is opposite the shorter side.

The bearing of $V$ from $W$ is $150^\circ+180^\circ=330^\circ$. Underwood lies anticlockwise from $WV$ (to the left when facing $V$ from $W$), so subtract.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Bearing of } U \text{ from } W &= 330^\circ-42.6^\circ \\ &\approx 287^\circ \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the helicopter should fly on a bearing of about } 287^\circ$$

meta.self_check: Verified with coordinates: W(98.3,-30.8), bearing W to U = 287.4 degrees.

Rules 1,3,4,6a,11,14,19,22.

parts.latex: Find the size of $\angle AOD$.
Find the area of triangle $AOB$, correct to the nearest square metre.
Richie stands at point $C$. Find the bearing of $O$ from where Richie is standing. Give your answer to the nearest degree.

solutions.latex:
$\angle AOD$ is made up of $\angle DON$ and $\angle NOA$.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle AOD&=\angle DON+\angle NOA\\&=60^\circ+50^\circ\\&=110^\circ\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the size of $\angle DON$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
$$\angle AOB=140^\circ-50^\circ=90^\circ$$
Use the area formula with two sides and the included angle.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Area}&=\dfrac{1}{2}\times 305\times 230\times \sin 90^\circ\\&=35\,075\text{ m}^2\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the size of $\angle AOB$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Let $\angle COB=\theta$. Apply the cosine rule in triangle $COB$.
$$\begin{aligned}\cos\theta&=\dfrac{230^2+245^2-300^2}{2\times 230\times 245}\\ \theta&=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{230^2+245^2-300^2}{2\times 230\times 245}\right)\\ \therefore\theta&\approx 78^\circ\quad\text{(to the nearest degree)}\end{aligned}$$
Hence the bearing of $C$ from $O$ is $140^\circ+78^\circ=218^\circ$.

The bearing of $O$ from $C$ is the reverse bearing, $218^\circ-180^\circ$.
$$\therefore\text{ the bearing of } O \text{ from } C \text{ is } 038^\circ$$
criteria: Finds the bearing of $C$ from $O$, or equivalent merit
Finds the size of $\angle COB$, or equivalent merit

Manavdeep leaves island $A$ in a boat and sails 164 km on a bearing of $070^\circ$ to island $B$. He then sails on a bearing of $194^\circ$ for 241 km to island $C$, as shown in the diagram.

figures.cap: bearings diagram: A to B 164 km on 070, B to C 241 km on 194

parts.latex: Show that the size of $\angle ABC=56^\circ$.
Using the cosine rule, find the distance from $A$ to $C$. Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.
Using the sine rule, calculate $\angle BCA$ to the nearest degree.
What is the bearing of $A$ from $C$ to the nearest degree?

solutions.latex:
The bearing $194^\circ$ is $180^\circ+14^\circ$, so the angle between the south line at $B$ and $BC$ is $14^\circ$.
$$180^\circ-110^\circ=70^\circ$$
As the source gives:
$$\begin{aligned} 194^\circ-180^\circ &= 14^\circ \\ 70^\circ-14^\circ &= 56^\circ \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \angle ABC=56^\circ$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us. Source working kept; the extra line I added about $110^\circ$ should be removed if unwanted. Diagram for solution (sketch_id 821_q23_s1) may be wanted.

solutions.latex:
Apply the cosine rule in triangle $ABC$ with $\angle ABC=56^\circ$, $AB=164$ and $BC=241$.
$$\begin{aligned} AC &= \sqrt{164^2+241^2-2\times 164\times 241\times\cos 56^\circ} \\ &= 201.9255\ldots \\ &\approx 202 \text{ km} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Apply the sine rule, with $\angle BCA$ opposite $AB=164$ and $\angle ABC=56^\circ$ opposite $AC\approx 202$.
$$\dfrac{\sin C}{164}=\dfrac{\sin 56^\circ}{202}$$
$$\begin{aligned} C &= \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{164\times\sin 56^\circ}{202}\right) \\ &= 42.305\ldots^\circ \\ &= 42^\circ 18'18.82'' \\ &\approx 42^\circ \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Sets up the sine rule correctly, or equivalent merit

meta.source_flag: Source writes the unknown angle as $A$ in the sine rule, but it is $\angle BCA$ (opposite $AB$); I labelled it $C$.

solutions.latex:
The bearing of $A$ from $C$ is found using the $42^\circ$ angle at $C$ and the $14^\circ$ angle between the north line at $C$ and $CB$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Bearing} &= 360^\circ-(42^\circ-14^\circ) \\ &= 332^\circ \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the angle between the north line and $CA$, or equivalent merit

7088.stem:
Angus and Bernie were camping at a site located at $P$. Angus walked from $P$ on a bearing of $040^\circ$ for 6 km to location $A$. Bernie walked on a bearing of $103^\circ$ from $P$ for 10 km to location $B$.

\exfigure{713_q13_1}

figures.cap: P with A at 6 km on bearing 040 and B at 10 km on bearing 103
solution sketch: annotated bearing diagram with 63 degrees, 9.03 km and bearing from A

parts.latex: Calculate the size of $\angle APB$.
Show that the distance of $AB$ is 9.03 km.
Find the true bearing of Bernie from Angus.

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned} \angle APB &= 103^\circ-40^\circ \\ &= 63^\circ \end{aligned}$$

$$\therefore \angle APB=63^\circ$$

Using the cosine rule in triangle $APB$:

$$\begin{aligned} AB^2 &= 6^2+10^2-2\times 6\times 10\cos 63^\circ \\ &\approx 81.5 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} AB &= \sqrt{81.5} \\ &= 9.0289\ldots \\ &\approx 9.03 \text{ km (2 d.p.)} \end{aligned}$$

Using the cosine rule in triangle $APB$ to find $\angle PAB$:

$$\cos\angle PAB=\dfrac{6^2+9.03^2-10^2}{2\times 6\times 9.03}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \angle PAB &= \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{6^2+9.03^2-10^2}{2\times 6\times 9.03}\right) \\ &= 80^\circ 41'3.08'' \end{aligned}$$

The bearing of $P$ from $A$ is $180^\circ+40^\circ=220^\circ$, so the bearing of $B$ from $A$ is found using the angle between $AP$ and $AB$:

$$80^\circ 41'-40^\circ=40^\circ 41'$$
$$180^\circ-40^\circ 41'=139^\circ 19'$$

\exfigure{713_q13_s1}

$$\therefore \text{the true bearing of Bernie from Angus is } 139^\circ 19'$$
criteria: Finds $\angle PAB$ and attempts the bearing, or equivalent merit
Substitutes correctly into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

7171.stem:
Robert walks 5.59 km from his house to the shop on a bearing of $063^\circ$. He then turns on a bearing of $124^\circ$ to walk to the post office, where he is 13.34 km from home.

\exfigure{714_q42_1}

figures.cap: bearings diagram House, Shop, Post office
solution sketch: bearings diagram with angles 117 and 119 marked

parts.latex: Show that $\angle HSP = 119^\circ$.
Find the bearing of Robert’s house from the post office. Give your answer correct to the nearest degree.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{714_q42_s1}

The angle between north and $HS$ extended backwards is $180 - 63 = 117^\circ$.
$$117 + 124 + \angle HSP = 360 \quad (\text{angles at a point})$$
$$\angle HSP + 241 = 360$$
$$\angle HSP = 360 - 241 = 119^\circ$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us. Kept guideline figure.

solutions.latex:
In triangle $HSP$, by the sine rule:
$$\dfrac{\sin \angle SPH}{5.59} = \dfrac{\sin 119^\circ}{13.34}$$
$$\sin \angle SPH = \dfrac{5.59 \sin 119^\circ}{13.34}$$
$$\angle SPH = 21^\circ$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Bearing} = 360 - 21 - 56 = 283^\circ$$

parts.latex:
The bearing of Isham's home from her friend Vanessa's home is $230^\circ$.

What is the bearing of Vanessa' home from Isham's home?

solutions.latex:
The bearing of the reverse direction differs by $180^\circ$, because the two north lines are parallel (co-interior angles).

Vanessa's home from Isham's home:
$$230^\circ - 180^\circ = 050^\circ$$
Hence the answer is B.

7545.stem:
The diagram below shows the plan for a triangular garden. Fence posts have been located at points $A$, $B$ and $C$. $AB$ is 40 m and $BC$ is 90 m. The bearing of $B$ from $A$ is $060^\circ$ and $\angle ABC$ is $120^\circ$

\exfigure{711_q30_1}

figures.cap: triangle ABC with north lines, AB 40 m, AC 115 m, angle at A 60 degrees, angle ABC 120 degrees
solution sketch: garden diagram annotated with angles 120 degrees, 90 m and alpha

parts.latex: What is the size of angle $\theta$ ?
What is the true bearing of point $A$ from point $C$?

solutions.latex:
$$\theta=120^\circ$$
\exfigure{711_q30_s1}

Apply the sine rule in triangle $ABC$, where $\alpha=\angle ACB$ and $AC=115$ m is the side opposite $\angle ABC$.
$$\dfrac{\sin\alpha}{40}=\dfrac{\sin120^\circ}{115}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \alpha &= \sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{40\sin120^\circ}{115}\right) \\ &\approx 17^\circ32' \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Bearing of } A \text{ from } C &= 360^\circ-(60^\circ+17^\circ32') \\ &\approx 282^\circ\text{T} \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
Ship $B$ is located on a bearing of $240^\circ$ from Ship A.

Which of the following diagrams shows this bearing?

solutions.latex:
A bearing is measured clockwise from north at the starting ship. Here it is the bearing of $B$ from $A$, so the north line and the angle must be at $A$.

A bearing of $240^\circ$ is more than $180^\circ$, so $B$ lies to the south-west of $A$.

Measured clockwise, $240^\circ$ is the same as $360^\circ - 240^\circ = 120^\circ$ anticlockwise from north, so the $120^\circ$ angle is on the west (left) side of the north line.

Options A and B have the $120^\circ$ angle on the east side (a bearing of $120^\circ$), and options B and D put the north line at $B$, which gives the bearing of $A$ from $B$.

Only diagram C has the north line at $A$, with $B$ to the south-west and $120^\circ$ anticlockwise from north.

So the correct diagram is option C.
